scope_reviewed: project/tests/test_npc_evidence_contract.py (full 705-line file, current working-tree bytes confirmed unchanged since the ruff pass per Main's second IRC note) plus scripts/validate_npc_goal_evidence.py and scripts/run_npc_goal_experiment.py consulted read-only for validation-contract semantics.

findings.issue: cases_by_id iteration vs zip(cases, assignments) truncation/misidentification
findings.evidence: Old code (git diff vs HEAD 25394a4) built records via `for case, assignment in zip(cases, assignments)`. For NPC-SCR1, make_assignments (scripts/run_npc_goal_experiment.py:359-402) expands 12 screening cases x ARMS(3) x repetitions(2) = 72 assignments, while `cases` has only 12 entries. zip() on (12-item, 72-item) lists silently truncates to 12 pairs, and all pairs after index 0 mismatch case identity against the assignment's actual case_id (assignments for case0 occupy indices 0-5, so zip pairs case1 with assignment1, which actually belongs to case0). Current code instead builds `cases_by_id = {case['id']: case for case in cases}` and `assignments_by_id = {assignment['assignment_id']: assignment for assignment in assignments}`, then iterates `for assignment in assignments` (all 72) looking up `cases_by_id[assignment['case_id']]` for each -- guaranteed-correct identity by construction (make_assignments sets case_id = case['id']). Post-loop `self.assertEqual([(row['assignment_id'], row['case_id']) for row in records], [(assignment['assignment_id'], assignment['case_id']) for assignment in assignments])` (lines ~244-247) independently re-verifies full-coverage, order-preserving, correct-identity mapping for every one of the 72 assignments. The second per-record loop building bootstrap/sidecar data (lines ~255-258) uses the identical id-based resolution, not positional zip. Arithmetic (12x3x2=72) and the pre-existing test_canonical_final_manifests_have_exact_arm_denominators (NPC-SCR1: P=24,R=24,O=24=72) corroborate the 72 count.

findings.issue: Restored mutation loop actually invokes each callback and checks intended rejection after an asserted valid baseline
findings.status: FIXED, verified correct -- this was the more severe defect: a vacuous (never-executed) negative test
findings.evidence: git diff shows the entire `for variant in ("arbitrary-count","omitted-duplicate","lane-swap"): with self.subTest(...): self._replay_mutation = variant; report, errors = self._validate_synthetic_mutation(mutate); self.assertFalse(report['valid']); self.assertTrue(any('replay' in error.lower() for error in errors), errors)` block is newly added (all '+' lines). In the prior committed version, `mutate(packet_dir)` was defined with full if/elif/else dispatch over the three mutation kinds but was never passed to any caller -- the test method had zero assertions and would trivially 'pass' under unittest without exercising any rejection logic at all. This is exactly the 'defined-but-never-executed' pattern named in the assignment. It is now genuinely restored: _validate_synthetic_mutation (lines ~382-388) first builds a fresh synthetic packet, asserts `self.assertTrue(baseline_report['valid'], baseline_errors)` BEFORE calling `mutate(packet_dir)`, then returns the post-mutation validate_packet() result -- i.e. baseline-valid-first, then-mutate, then-check ordering is correct for all three variants. The dispatcher's old silent catch-all `else:` (which previously coerced any unrecognized variant into lane-swap behavior) is now `elif self._replay_mutation == 'lane-swap': ... else: raise AssertionError(f'unknown replay mutation: {self._replay_mutation}')`, closing the silent-miscoercion risk this family of bug represents.

findings.issue: Packet-local bootstrap input/sidecar receipts bound to current hashes, explicitly engine not_run/non-publication, no fake actual-engine success
findings.evidence: config_digest/project_digest/schema_digest/frozen_policy are computed live at test-run time via canonical_config_hash(P/...), source_project_config_hash(P), sha256_file(P/...), policy_hash(P) -- i.e. actual current repo bytes, not hardcoded/stale values (consistent with Main's note that the runtime-hash helper is intentionally dynamic pre-005-freeze). Each record's injected `engine` block sets top-level `available: False, status: 'not_run'`, `experiment: {available: False, status: 'not_run'}`, `replay: {available: False, status: 'not_run', valid: False, rows: 0, model_calls: 0}` -- explicitly non-publication, no claimed native-engine success. Only `bootstrap.status='completed'` is asserted, which is literally true (the test itself wrote the bootstrap input file and sidecar trace file to disk) and is clearly distinguished from `experiment`/replay (the actual Godot invocation), which stays not_run. Underlying execute_assignment() record carries `status='assigned_failure'` and `failure=[{category:'engine_gate_failure', code:'synthetic_admission', error:'synthetic'}]` (scripts/run_npc_goal_experiment.py ~line 1521+), i.e. the synthetic short-circuit is labeled as synthetic/non-production throughout, not silently recast as success. record_sha256 is correctly recomputed after the engine-field substitution (self-consistent hash).

findings.issue: Publication-negative tests exercise intended boundaries, not unrelated missing-bootstrap/source failures
findings.evidence: publishable = run_mode=='publish' and packet=='NPC-SCR1' and not errors; _validate_publish_records only executes its per-record checks when run_mode=='publish' and packet=='NPC-SCR1', otherwise returns immediately -- so the dry_run test (run_mode mutated on both source-manifest.json and aggregate.json in lockstep, avoiding the 'aggregate run_mode does not match source manifest' mismatch error) triggers zero publish-record checks, and `self.assertFalse(any('run_mode' in error for error in errors))` is satisfied for the correct reason (dry_run is an accepted run_mode value, not an error state) rather than an incidental match. For the publish-mode test, every synthetic record has `cli_exec_attempts=[]` (injected admission short-circuit never reaches real CLI-exec code), so for arm=='P' assignments (24 of 72 for NPC-SCR1) the validator fires `'record[i]: publish P assignment must have exactly one codex exec attempt'` -- confirmed via source read that this is the only 'exec'-substring-bearing error reachable here (the sibling 'cli_exec_attempts must be a list' branch cannot fire since attempts IS a list; the 'policy-bound' branch is mutually exclusive with the triggered one). R/O arm assignments correctly produce zero errors since model_calls==0==len(attempts) with attempts falsy. This is the intended injected-execution-attempt boundary, not a bootstrap/source hash false failure.

findings.issue: verified-run-005 pointer correctness while NEW005 data intentionally awaits collection
findings.anchor: tests/test_npc_evidence_contract.py:139-154 (_verified_dir, _copy_verified, _copy_portable_project); scripts/validate_npc_goal_evidence.py (_path, validate_packet default, main()); scripts/run_npc_goal_experiment.py main()
findings.evidence: Confirmed via filesystem check: research/academic-pipeline/npc-goal-recovery/verified-run-005 does not exist (verified-run-004 does, untracked). grep across all three reviewed files for 'verified-run-00[1-4]' returns zero matches -- the 003->005 pointer rename is complete and consistent project-wide within scope, not a partial migration. Every test method that calls _copy_verified()/_copy_portable_project()/self._verified_dir() directly (test_canonical_final_manifests_have_exact_arm_denominators, test_canonical_packet_survives_relocation_and_rejects_input_substitution, test_missing_p_execution_rows_reject_publication, test_record_cannot_rebind_p_assignment_to_rule_arm, test_rehashed_aggregate_counters_cannot_fake_valid_counts, test_embedded_native_trace_must_match_packet_scoped_sidecar, test_native_input_path_must_stay_inside_packet_and_bind_record, test_completed_record_cannot_rebind_request_id) will currently error against the missing directory. Per the assignment's acceptance criteria this is explicitly NOT required to pass before NEW005 collection, and EvidenceTester2's receipt (codex-evidence-contract-repair.json) and Main's own focused-command list confirm only the three in-scope, non-005-dependent tests were run and asserted green (exit 0, 3 tests, 2.677s). The pointer itself -- the string value these helpers resolve to -- is correct for the post-freeze state; its current non-existence is a data-collection-timing fact, not a code defect.

defect_family_sweep: Read all 705 lines end to end looking for other 'defined but never invoked' callback/loop patterns beyond the scoped zip/mutation-loop family. test_receipt_rejects_empty_missing_duplicate_and_relocated_entries (line ~421), test_relocated_packet_file_corruption_is_not_hidden_by_receipt (~445), test_publication_requires_publish_mode/test_publication_requires_injected_execution_attempt (~456,470), and test_canonical_packet_survives_relocation_and_rejects_input_substitution (~517-580) all define a mutate()/variant body AND drive it with an actual loop or direct call that reaches an assertion -- no other vacuous-test instances found in this class. The remaining bare `else:` at line ~432 (test_receipt_rejects_...) is pre-existing, not touched by this diff, and is exhaustively reached only by the loop's literal 4th variant string ('relocated') -- not a silent-miscoercion risk like the one fixed, since there is no unlisted 5th variant anywhere in the calling loop.
non_blocking_notes: test_publication_requires_injected_execution_attempt's mutate() sets payload['cli_exec_attempt_count']=0 on source-manifest.json/aggregate.json; grep confirms validate_npc_goal_evidence.py never reads this field anywhere. It is dead/decorative in this test -- the real enforcement path is the per-record cli_exec_attempts list via _validate_publish_records. Harmless, not a correctness defect, but could be dropped for clarity.

The surviving bare `else:` in test_receipt_rejects_empty_missing_duplicate_and_relocated_entries (line ~432) is correct today but, unlike the now-fixed replay-mutation dispatcher, has no explicit 'raise AssertionError on unknown variant' guard. Not part of this diff or this defect family's scope; flagged only as an opportunistic future hardening, not required for this approval.
